page_text:
Write HTML online, with a live preview

The HTML Editor shows your code and the page side by side. Whatever you type appears in the preview right away - headings, lists, tables, pictures and all your CSS - and a click on anything in the preview takes you to its place in the code. You can also edit the text right in the preview. That makes it quick to build landing pages, newsletters, articles and forms without installing anything.

Everything runs in your browser. Your pages are kept there, not on our server, and there is no sign-up and no advertising.

What the editor can do

Code with highlighting

Tags, attributes, entities, comments and the CSS and JavaScript inside the page in their own colors, line numbers, end tags that close by themselves, and tidy indentation at a click.

A safe live preview

The page as the browser shows it, in a frame where scripts and on… attributes never run and links do not navigate. Check it at full width, tablet or phone size.

Edit in the preview

Click a heading or a paragraph in the preview and type: the change goes into the code, with &, < and > written as entities.

Problems at a glance

Unclosed or misnested tags, unknown elements, pictures without alt, missing files and ids used twice - each with its line.

Pictures, stylesheets, fonts

Drag files into the editor and use them by name: <img src="logo.png">, <link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css">. They are kept with the page in your browser.

Export

The .html file, one HTML file with every file inside, a ZIP with the files, a PDF through the print dialog, or the plain text.

How it works

  1. Start - choose a template under "New", open an .html file or a ZIP, or paste HTML code.
  2. Write - type in the code; the preview follows. Use "Insert" for lists, tables, media and form fields.
  3. Export - save the .html, a ZIP with its files, or a PDF.

Use the editor on your own website

Put the editor into your own website with an iframe or in a window of its own. Your page hands it the document, gets every change and every save back, and can let an AI send its results to your server. No sign-up, no key.

Embed the editor on your website →

Frequently asked questions

Is my page uploaded?

No. The editor runs in your browser and keeps your pages there, not on our server. A page goes to a server only if you set up a webhook to your own server, if a website that embeds the editor saves it on its own server, or if another website opens it here with a form (post.php) - our server then passes it straight to your browser without storing it. As on any website, the server logs each visit, and we count page views anonymously - see the privacy policy.

Does JavaScript run in the preview?

No. The preview shows the HTML and CSS of the page, but scripts and on… attributes never run, and links do not navigate. That keeps the editor safe with any page you open. The code keeps its scripts, so the exported page works as before.

How do I add pictures and stylesheets?

Drag or paste them into the editor, or add them in the Files tab on the right. They are stored with the page in your browser and used by their name, for example <img src="logo.png"> or <link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css">.

How do I get a PDF?

Click "Export", choose PDF and click "Print / Save as PDF". In the print dialog choose "Save as PDF" as the printer.

Where are my documents saved?

Only in your browser. Click the folder button at the top left (My documents) to open, rename, duplicate, download or delete them. Clearing your browser's site data removes them, so download the ones you want to keep - or let the editor send them to your own server ("Save to server").

Can an AI write in the HTML Editor?

Yes, any AI - ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Copilot or the AI in your coding tool. Click "AI Assistant", then "Copy prompt", paste it into your AI and say what it should write. The AI answers with a link; click it and the page appears in your editor. "Undo" takes every change back.

Can I use the editor on my own website?

Yes. Embed it with an iframe and exchange documents with postMessage, or let it send every saved version to your server with a webhook. See Use the editor on your own website for examples.

Does the HTML Editor cost anything?

No. The editor is free, without ads and without sign-up.

embed.h1: Embed the HTML Editor in your website
embed.intro: For developers: how to put the HTML Editor into your own page - in an iframe, in a window of its own or as a read-only viewer - and how documents, saves and AI results travel between the editor and your server. You need no sign-up and no key from us.
embed.body:
Any https page (and localhost) can embed the editor with an <iframe> and ?embed=1 - no sign-up, no key. Embedded, the editor hides the page text and shows a Save button. There are four ways to get the document in and out.

1. Open a file from a link, save to your server

src= opens a file (your server must allow CORS), webhook= makes "Save" (Ctrl+S) send the document to that address. Add &auto to save after every change.

<iframe src="https://html.giit.ch/?embed=1&src=https://your-site.com/pages/offer.html&webhook=https://your-site.com/save.php"
        allow="clipboard-write" style="width:100%;height:800px;border:0"></iframe>

The webhook gets a POST with JSON { editor, event: "save", id, name, content, assets, updated }. A link carries no token (it would end up in server logs and the browser history), so a webhook in the address suits a save address that needs none, for example on localhost or in your intranet. For a public server, hand the webhook over with a token in htmleditor:load (hook: { url, token }) and check it, as this small PHP script does:

<?php
header('Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://html.giit.ch');
header('Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Content-Type, Authorization');
header('Access-Control-Allow-Methods: POST, OPTIONS');
if ($_SERVER['REQUEST_METHOD'] === 'OPTIONS') exit;
if (($_SERVER['HTTP_AUTHORIZATION'] ?? '') !== 'Bearer SECRET') { http_response_code(403); exit; }
$d = json_decode(file_get_contents('php://input'), true);
$name = preg_replace('/[^\w\- ]/u', '_', $d['name']);
file_put_contents(__DIR__ . "/pages/$name.html", $d['content']);
echo '{"ok":true}';

2. Your page holds the document (postMessage)

The editor says htmleditor:ready, your page answers with htmleditor:load, the editor reports htmleditor:loaded, htmleditor:change on real edits and htmleditor:save when the user saves. Your page may send htmleditor:get (the current state) or htmleditor:save (press Save). Saving then goes through your own login and session.

<iframe id="ed" src="https://html.giit.ch/?embed=1" allow="clipboard-write" style="width:100%;height:800px;border:0"></iframe>
<script>
const ed = document.getElementById('ed');
const ORIGIN = 'https://html.giit.ch';

addEventListener('message', async e => {
  if (e.source !== ed.contentWindow || e.origin !== ORIGIN) return;
  const m = e.data;
  if (m.type === 'htmleditor:ready') {              // the editor is ready: hand it the document
    ed.contentWindow.postMessage({
      type: 'htmleditor:load',
      name: 'Offer',
      content: await (await fetch('/pages/offer.html')).text(),
      assets: { 'logo.png': 'data:image/png;base64,…' }   // optional files
    }, ORIGIN);
  }
  if (m.type === 'htmleditor:change') document.title = '● not saved';   // a real edit
  if (m.type === 'htmleditor:save') {               // the user clicked "Save"
    await fetch('/api/save', { method: 'POST', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
      body: JSON.stringify({ name: m.name, content: m.content, assets: m.assets }) });
    document.title = 'Saved';
  }
});

// A save button on your own page: the answer comes as htmleditor:save
function saveNow() { ed.contentWindow.postMessage({ type: 'htmleditor:get' }, ORIGIN); }
</script>

AI Assistant inside your page: it works in the frame too. With allow="clipboard-write" on the iframe, "Copy prompt" uses the clipboard directly (otherwise the editor falls back to the old copy command, or shows the prompt to copy by hand). A link the AI sends cannot reach an editor inside another website, so the editor tells the AI and the user to paste the AI's whole answer into the editor instead - or open the editor in a window of its own.

3. In a window of its own

window.open("https://html.giit.ch/?embed=window", "htmleditor-17") opens the full editor in its own window and speaks the same messages with window.opener. Links from an AI reach it there. htmleditor:load may also carry context: { host, title, rules } - the AI prompt then says where the document belongs and follows your rules - and hook: { url, token, assets: false }, a webhook for this document only that is never stored. Closing the window with unsaved changes sends htmleditor:closing.

4. AI through your own server

Hand the editor your own prompt, an address on your site and a key for this editor session. The AI dialog then shows "Connected to" your site, what you tell the AI, and the choice change the current document or make a new one; Copy prompt puts it all together. The AI posts its result with the key to your server, and your page opens it in the editor - a new document opens separately and stays in the user's browser. One key per editor session: it stays valid while the editor is open, and only while it has none the editor asks for it with htmleditor:key-request. The editor never sends the key itself and never stores it; the address must be https on your own host or a subdomain of it.

const key = async () => (await fetch('/api/ai-key.php?doc=17')).json();   // one key per editor session
const k = await key();
ed.contentWindow.postMessage({ type: 'htmleditor:load', name: 'Offer', content, ai: {
  label: 'My Site', prompt: 'Keep the [[placeholders]]. Write in German.',
  endpoint: 'https://your-site.com/api/ai-result.php', key: k.key } }, ORIGIN);
// remember the id from htmleditor:loaded and ignore change/save/closing with another id
// only while the editor has no key:
if (m.type === 'htmleditor:key-request') { const k = await key(); ed.contentWindow.postMessage({ type: 'htmleditor:ai', key: k.key }, ORIGIN); }
// while the editor is open, tell your server every minute; closing the editor or the page voids the key
setInterval(() => fetch('/api/ai-key.php?alive=' + k.key.slice(0, 8)), 60000);
// your server has a result (polling, SSE …): target is "current" or "new"
ed.contentWindow.postMessage({ type: 'htmleditor:load', name: 'Offer', content: draft, from: 'ai', target }, ORIGIN);
<?php // api/ai-key.php - the key of this editor session of the logged-in user (your page calls it)
session_start();                                     // check that the user may edit this document
$key = bin2hex(random_bytes(24));
$_SESSION['ai'][hash('sha256', $key)] = ['doc' => (int)$_GET['doc'], 'seen' => time()];  // or in your database; ?alive= sets seen again
echo json_encode(['key' => $key]);

<?php // api/ai-result.php - the AI posts here (no CORS headers: AIs call it from a server)
$key = preg_replace('/^Bearer\s+/', '', $_SERVER['HTTP_AUTHORIZATION'] ?? '');
$row = find_key(hash('sha256', $key));               // your database: not voided, seen in the last 3 minutes
if (!$row) { http_response_code(401); exit('{"ok":false,"error":"key not valid"}'); }
$d = json_decode(file_get_contents('php://input', false, null, 0, 2000000), true);
save_draft($row['doc'], $d['content'], $d['target'] === 'new' ? 'new' : 'current');   // your page shows it with htmleditor:load
echo '{"ok":true}';

Make keys with at least 128 random bits, store only their hash, bind each to the logged-in user, the document and this editor session, make one per session, keep it valid only while your page reports the session as open, and void it when the editor or the page closes.

Your own AI dialog and answering instructions: with dialog: "page" in ai, a click on AI Assistant sends htmleditor:ai-click with a request id; answer { type: "htmleditor:ai-click", request, handled: true } within 300 ms and show your own dialog - otherwise the editor opens its own. answer: "…" puts your text in place of the "HOW TO ANSWER" part of the copied prompt ("none" leaves the part out, "" brings the editor's part back); the prompt then carries no key. When your server gives no key, answer htmleditor:key-request with { type: "htmleditor:ai", decline: true, message: "…" }: the editor stops waiting at once and shows your message after your host - write it in your page's language. In the prompt the document always stands in a fence longer than any run of backticks in it, marked as data.

The whole protocol is in llms.txt - give it to an AI and it builds the connection for your system. The other giit editors work the same way with their own prefix - editors.giit.ch.

Show a document read-only (viewer)

?viewer=1 shows only the finished document: no code, no tools, nothing can be changed, and nothing is stored in the browser. The document comes from a link (#b64=, ?src=), from your page with htmleditor:load, or by POST as a normal form to post.php: the field content as text or b64 as base64, optionally name, at most 20 MB of text.

<form method="post" action="https://html.giit.ch/post.php?viewer=1" target="_blank">
  <input type="hidden" name="name" value="Report">
  <input type="hidden" name="b64" value="…">
  <button>Open</button>
</form>

Without viewer=1 the document opens in the normal editor. Either way it is kept in memory only: it is not stored on the server and does not join "My documents". Opened directly, the viewer says that the content comes from a third party.

Templates with placeholders

When your server fills placeholders into the HTML before the page is used, add template=mustache for {{name}}, {{#name}} … {{/name}} and {{^name}} … {{/name}}, or template=angle for <<name>> and <<?name>> … <</?name>>. The list of problems reads every tag as one placeholder and reports a section left open, a stray end tag, an end tag in the wrong order and a tag with an unknown sign; the code shows the tags as written.

Send your placeholders with examples and example pictures, and the preview shows the page filled with them: sections by their example state, a list once per example row, pictures from assets (PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP, at most 20 and 40 MB). A placeholder without an example shows its label in brackets, such as [Name]. The switch Template in the preview’s bar shows the tags as text, Examples brings the examples back; the box Placeholders below the code puts a tag at the cursor. Examples are shown as text, stay in memory only and never reach your page: saving, change, get, the webhook and every export of the code carry the template as written; print and PDF follow the view shown and name it in their title. An address that holds a placeholder is never loaded, also when it is filled with an example.

frame.contentWindow.postMessage({ type: 'htmleditor:template',
  placeholders: [
    { name: 'name', kind: 'value', label: 'Name', example: 'John Doe' },
    { name: 'logo', kind: 'image', label: 'Logo', image: 'logo.png' },
    { name: 'hasNote', kind: 'section', label: 'With a note', shown: true },
    { name: 'items', kind: 'list', label: 'Items',
      fields: [ { name: 'label', label: 'Item' }, { name: 'quantity', label: 'Quantity' } ],
      rows: [ { label: 'Chair', quantity: '2' }, { label: 'Table', quantity: '1' } ] } ],
  assets: { 'logo.png': 'data:image/png;base64,…' } }, ORIGIN);
// or the same object as the field template of htmleditor:load; { type: 'htmleditor:template', clear: true } ends it
<iframe src="https://html.giit.ch/?embed=1&template=mustache" allow="clipboard-write" style="width:100%;height:800px;border:0"></iframe>
